seo.title: Suzy Says Game: Overview, Guides and More Horror Games
seo.description: Meet the Suzy Says game, compare Windows and Android editions, and find focused player guides. Explore eight more horror games with their own rules and stories.

blocks.text: Suzy Says is MOONBIT��s first-person horror game about a mysterious interactive DVD waiting at home after an evening with a friend. Its cheerful host turns a familiar listening game into an unsettling encounter. The television, a colored floor mat and an ordinary house establish the scene; understanding what the host asks is part of the tension. This overview avoids later story events so you can decide where to start without learning an ending.

Listening matters before moving. In the original game, an instruction qualified by the host��s name is different from the same action requested without those words. The challenge is to distinguish what you heard from what you expected. The focused guides below explain that distinction and prepare the Windows controls; this page introduces the game and points you toward the right kind of help.

blocks.alt: Suzy appearing on the television in a purple bedroom
blocks.caption: Keep the television in view while listening to the current instruction.

blocks.text: The original Windows release is available through MOONBIT on itch.io. The base download and Full version are different choices: Full includes endless mode and a secret ending. Check the creator��s current listing when choosing a download rather than assuming that every copy includes every mode. A separate official Android app is also available, with its own on-screen interface.

Windows uses WASD to move, Space to jump and C to crouch. Those keys describe that edition, not every game hosted under a similar name. Android uses a different input method. Choose the edition you intend to use before following instructions, and read its own prompts rather than translating keyboard actions into assumed touch gestures.

The third-party browser player above has not been verified as the original Suzy Says release. Loading a frame or expanding it to fullscreen does not establish its identity, edition or included modes. Treat the player��s own controls separately from the Windows guidance on this site. The original game includes flashing lights, jumpscares and unsettling themes; read its warning before continuing.

blocks.caption: Locate the colored pads before matching a command to its target.

content.heading: Find the guide for your next step

blocks.text: For the listening rule, use the command guide. It compares qualified and unqualified instructions, works through a crouch example and separates a missed rule from a missed input. This keeps the explanation together in one place instead of repeating the full exercise here.

For a first Windows session, use the setup guide. It covers choosing an edition, preparing the downloaded files, checking movement keys and selecting readable subtitles. It also explains how to distinguish a setup problem from a working game that is waiting for your next action. Neither guide is a complete ending walkthrough.

blocks.alt: The colorful Suzy Says DVD box held in a floral-wallpaper hallway
blocks.caption: The DVD box introduces the game within the house.

content.heading: Eight more unsettling games to explore

blocks.text: The six featured cards above offer different kinds of horror: desktop investigation, unsettling tests, an unusual house tour, a short first-person encounter and a circus performance. Exhibit of Sorrows and Burger & Frights are included alongside last seen online and the other selected games. Open an individual page for that game��s own premise, controls and help; its rules do not carry over from Suzy Says.

The More Games section contains the two titles not already shown in the featured selection. The full games list brings all eight together. These are recommendations, not official Suzy Says editions, and the selection does not claim that they were released on different dates. Choose the experience that interests you rather than treating a recommendation as another chapter of the same story.
